**Finding: compliant (at fallback).**

- **§26 (p0093)** — "governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law)" → California is an accepted fallback governing law.
- **§27 (p0094)** — disputes "resolved solely and exclusively in the state or federal courts located within San Luis Obispo County, California," with consent to jurisdiction and waiver of venue/forum non conveniens objections → the corresponding California courts, matching the fallback forum element.
- No arbitration clause exists anywhere in the document (searched; §§13–30 reviewed in full), so the walk-away trigger (foreign seat or non-accepted home jurisdiction with exclusive foreign venue) is not present.

Because the bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, no redline was proposed — we do not upgrade to the preferred New York law / New York County forum merely to reach preferred wording. The only sub-preferred points, noted rather than flagged, are the accepted-but-not-preferred California choice of law and the Vendor-convenient San Luis Obispo County venue.
